prompt_en: Create a photorealistic science-editorial scene inside a storm-lit mobile genomics clinic built into an alpine seed vault. An unmistakably adult woman derived from the supplied portrait’s oval face, brown eyes, and long dark wavy hair works as a field geneticist at a multispectral tissue scanner with paired slides. Her body is anatomically coherent and naturally human; her complete human silhouette and normal human hands and organs remain visibly coherent. She places one normal hand beneath the scanner. Beside her, a translucent anatomical projection shows two interwoven fluorescent cell-line distributions in different colors across the same organs, visibly integrated across the same organs of the human body. A dual-origin cell lineage diagram makes the scientific cellular-lineage reading unmistakable. Seed drawers, wet rock, cable bundles, and lightning beyond a narrow window surround her. Frame a three-quarter environmental portrait with a triangular reading path from her attentive face to the scanning hand and then to the complete projected organ map. Cool laboratory panels and white storm flashes share one believable direction, casting related reflections across skin, field coat, scanner glass, and damp stone.
negative_en: excessive HDR, over-processed retouching, 3D render look, low resolution, fake-looking background, illustration look, distorted fingers, broken facial features, cartoon style

decisions.rationale: Storm-linked laboratory illumination better supports the frozen setting.
A causal triangular hierarchy is more useful than a generic grid placement.
Full-body emphasis would reduce the organ-map and scanner evidence.
The precise scanning action should govern posture rather than an assertive stance.
The final gaze remains subordinate to scanner work and scientific legibility.
Three-quarter environmental coverage better preserves body coherence and clinic context.
